verdict.rationale: iTerm2's shell integration tracks where the shell prompt is and places marks at each prompt. Users can jump to previous and next prompts with ⇧⌘↑ and ⇧⌘↓, and Copy Mode also works with marks to jump between command prompts. missing for 10: in-depth documentation of mark-navigation behavior (e.g. custom or trigger-set marks, scrollback limits), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can jump between prompts and command marks in my scrollback thanks to shell integration

citations.quote: you can easily navigate to previous shell prompts with ⇧⌘↑ and ⇧⌘↓
Works with marks to jump between command prompts.
iTerm2 can integrate with your shell so it knows where your shell prompt is, what commands you're entering
